segments.text: Please take a look at this incredible article from Atmos Earth
which details how indigenous leaders in the Pacific
are going to be issuing a declaration calling for whales
to be treated as legal persons.
And this declaration will call not only for treating
and recognizing whales as legal persons
with inherent rights, but also recognizing
a freedom of movement, a healthy environment,
and the ability to thrive alongside humanity
as rights of whales.
This concept was inspired by a similar law in New Zealand
which granted legal personhood to the Te Urewera Forest
and reflects the growing respect for indigenous knowledge
systems and their significance in environmental protection
on a grand scale.
In international law, this concept
is called rights of nature.
And it's this idea that nature has rights
and that the legal system should acknowledge
and protect those rights so that nature can continue
to be healthy and to regenerate
as a lawyer who was trained
in a Western legal tradition
and also a resident of a high emitting country.
I think it's absolutely imperative
that we consider ideas and concepts like this
and seek to integrate them where we can
in order to protect nature
and ultimately to protect ourselves.

transcript_full: Please take a look at this incredible article from Atmos Earth which details how indigenous leaders in the Pacific are going to be issuing a declaration calling for whales to be treated as legal persons. And this declaration will call not only for treating and recognizing whales as legal persons with inherent rights, but also recognizing a freedom of movement, a healthy environment, and the ability to thrive alongside humanity as rights of whales. This concept was inspired by a similar law in New Zealand which granted legal personhood to the Te Urewera Forest and reflects the growing respect for indigenous knowledge systems and their significance in environmental protection on a grand scale. In international law, this concept is called rights of nature. And it's this idea that nature has rights and that the legal system should acknowledge and protect those rights so that nature can continue to be healthy and to regenerate as a lawyer who was trained in a Western legal tradition and also a resident of a high emitting country. I think it's absolutely imperative that we consider ideas and concepts like this and seek to integrate them where we can in order to protect nature and ultimately to protect ourselves.
